meta.doctrine: Patterns move HYPOTHESIS → ACTIVE → STRESSED → CONFIRMED or BROKEN. A CONFIRMED pattern is load-bearing for analysis; a BROKEN pattern must never be silently reused. Every state change carries the evidence that caused it.

patterns.name: IRGC overrides the diplomatic track
patterns.rule: Trust Khamenei Telegram for operational intent; treat Araghchi/MFA as diplomatic narrative only.
patterns.evidence: IRGC publicly overrode the FM since Apr 2026 (UK Commons Library). Escalated 8 Jul: Witkoff and Kushner told Trump that Araghchi could not guarantee the IRGC would stop firing on shipping — and the renewed US strikes followed directly from that report (Israel Hayom). The split is no longer just an Iran-reading problem; it now drives US targeting decisions.

history.note: IRGC publicly contradicts FM on Hormuz
UK Commons Library confirms Mojtaba-Pezeshkian divergence on MOU
Split becomes a US casus belli via Witkoff/Kushner report

patterns.name: Iran signals before acting
patterns.rule: Assume Iranian kinetic action can come with zero prior signal. Absence of warning is not absence of intent.
patterns.evidence: Broken 18 Apr (IRGC fired without VHF warning). Re-validated 11 Jul: the GFS Galaxy was hit and disabled with a crew member missing — and Iran itself styled the strike a ‘warning shot.’ The warning IS the strike now.

history.note: VHF warnings preceded interceptions
Fire without warning
GFS Galaxy: the ‘warning shot’ disables the ship

patterns.name: Lebanon drives Hormuz re-closures
patterns.rule: Check the Lebanon front on every Hormuz event — but no longer assume it is the only driver.
patterns.evidence: Every re-closure through June traced to Lebanon (it is MOU Point 1). The 11 Jul closure declaration broke the chain: it traced to route enforcement (GFS Galaxy / southern-lane jurisdiction), not Lebanon. The Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire (19 Jun) is holding but fragile — Israel refuses withdrawal (Katz: security zones ‘for an unlimited period’). Downgraded CONFIRMED → STRESSED: the route war is now an independent closure driver.

history.note: Two re-closures trace to Lebanon
MOU makes Lebanon Point 1
First closure NOT traced to Lebanon — route enforcement instead

patterns.name: Trump maximal rhetoric, preserved off-ramp
patterns.rule: Never read Trump’s rhetoric as policy. Read the delegation manifest instead.
patterns.evidence: Upgraded ACTIVE → CONFIRMED 11 Jul on the cleanest instance yet: within hours of ‘1000 missiles locked and loaded’ and declaring the MOU dead, the most senior US team of the war (Vance, Rubio, Witkoff, Kushner) was dispatched toward Muscat. The rhetoric and the off-ramp are the same policy.

history.note: ‘It’s over’ / ‘scum’ while talks continue
Ceasefire ‘over’ at NATO; talks not terminated
Decimation threats + most senior delegation of the war, same day

patterns.name: Iran floats maximal options, executes calibrated ones
patterns.rule: Stated options (NPT, Bab-el-Mandeb) are bargaining inventory, not warning orders — but the calibration ceiling is rising.
patterns.evidence: Held in form on 11 Jul: NPT withdrawal and Bab-el-Mandeb (floated 8 Jul) stayed unexecuted; Iran instead closed its own strait — the maximal option fully inside its control. Marked STRESSED because ‘calibrated’ now includes a formal closure declaration: the gap between floated and executed options is narrowing with each cycle.

history.note: Bab-el-Mandeb threatened repeatedly, never executed
NPT + Bab-el-Mandeb floated as options
Executed option (closure) is itself near-maximal

patterns.name: Israel re-enters when US-Iran talks stall
patterns.rule: Watch for T2 confirmation of Israeli force movement whenever Muscat/Doha stalls. Israeli-official leaks during negotiations are also pressure instruments.
patterns.evidence: New 11 Jul: Ynet (‘more serious than any other time in the past’) and ToI report Israel preparing to rejoin strikes as talks make little headway — all Israeli-official sourcing, no T2 confirmation. Test: does a package launch while the US team is physically in Muscat? A launch would confirm; a quiet stand-down as talks progress would suggest the leaks were leverage.

history.note: First explicit re-entry signalling since the MOU

patterns.name: Strikes and talks run as parallel tracks, not alternatives
patterns.rule: Grade the kinetic and diplomatic tracks separately — but do not assume the diplomatic track is durable. It can break while the kinetic one accelerates.
patterns.evidence: Proposed 12 Jul (three strike rounds + senior delegations at once). Stressed 13 Jul: the tracks diverged rather than ran parallel — the US went to Round 4 (140 targets, sea-drone debut) on the SAME day the Muscat talks collapsed with nothing agreed and each side blamed the other in public. Parallelism held as a description of the week, but the diplomatic rail is no longer load-bearing; ‘grade separately’ now means being willing to mark one track BROKEN while the other runs hot.

history.note: Three strike rounds + senior delegations in the same week
Round 4 accelerates as Muscat talks collapse — tracks diverge, not parallel

patterns.name: Iran deliberately exempts the UAE from retaliation rounds
patterns.rule: UAE quiet ≠ UAE safe. Track the exemption itself as a signal: its end would mark a strategic decision, not an accident.
patterns.evidence: New 12 Jul: this round Iran struck Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Jordan — but not the UAE, despite the UAE being the war’s most-targeted state pre-MOU (1,800+ projectiles). Possible drivers: reconstruction-fund economics, Abu Dhabi back-channel, or target saturation elsewhere. Watch UAE MOD/WAM language for the first crack.

history.note: Four states hit this round; UAE conspicuously excluded
Sixth straight day: Round-4 retaliation hit Bahrain/Kuwait/Jordan (±Qatar/Oman) — UAE still untouched
